title: Anarchy in the U.K.
headline: 'Anarchist' was the best rhyme Johnny Rotten could find
caption:
Fifty years ago today the Sex Pistols put out "Anarchy in the U.K.", and John Lydon, the Johnny Rotten who wrote and sang it, has spent years saying he was never an anarchist.

The writer Jon Savage thinks some of the ideas came from Vivienne Westwood, who ran the Sex shop with McLaren, and the designer Jamie Reid, and that Lydon turned what they fed him into his own lyric. Malcolm McLaren, the band's manager, called the song "a call to arms to the kids who believe that rock and roll was taken away from them."

In 2012 Lydon pointed out he'd also sung Pretty Vacant: "I'm not pretty and I'm not vacant."

comment: About the song, when Rotten sings "I use the enemy," it's a deliberate play on "I use the NME," the British weekly music paper.
